new.title: Manifest schema v1 — review and sign off
new.body:
Schema v1 is drafted and decided — 116 columns, stage ownership defined, code in `src/schema/`. I made the calls so we could move; this is your pass to disagree.

**Docs:** [https://github.com/terbe2022/RIMS-Archival-Project-/blob/main/docs/W1_manifest_schema_v1.md](https://github.com/terbe2022/RIMS-Archival-Project-/blob/main/docs/W1_manifest_schema_v1.md)
**Code:** [manifest.py](https://github.com/terbe2022/RIMS-Archival-Project-/blob/main/src/schema/manifest.py) · [validate.py](https://github.com/terbe2022/RIMS-Archival-Project-/blob/main/src/schema/validate.py)

### Worth arguing about specifically

- **One row per path, never collapsed.** A file in three places is three archival facts. Dedupe is a decision (`duplicate_of`), not a representation. Costs rows; keeps provenance.
- **`file_uid` is deterministic** — blake2b of `source_id + path_norm`. Re-crawling yields identical keys, so generations join cleanly. The catch: a wrong `source_id` means a full re-crawl.
- **Per-stage status columns**, null = not reached. Makes `WHERE s03_status IS NULL` the work queue.
- **Text and embeddings live outside the manifest**, pointers only. 384-dim vectors at 5M rows is 7.5 GB in a column almost nothing reads.
- **`layer` is derived, never authored** — recomputed from decision columns so it cannot drift.

### Checklist

- [ ] Read the schema doc end to end
- [ ] Run `validate.py` against the fixture
- [ ] Raise anything you disagree with in this thread
- [ ] Sign the worksheet

Two bugs already found and fixed while testing, both worth understanding — they are the kind that hide until they are expensive. NaN is truthy in Python, so `if row.get("duplicate_of")` classified **every** row as layer 0; triage would have looked like it was rejecting everything. And building ~100 columns one at a time fragments the DataFrame — fine at 5 rows, awful at 5 million.

new.title: Build the 50-row test fixture
new.body:
`tests/fixtures/manifest_50.parquet` — synthetic, committed, safe in a public repo.

Must cover: every format class, every status value, every path flag, duplicates, archive children at depths 1–3, rows at each layer, and suspect dates (epoch zero, pre-1980, future).

- [ ] Fixture generated by a committed script, not by hand
- [ ] `validate.report()` passes on it
- [ ] A deliberately broken variant that trips each validation rule

Small task, disproportionate value: it lets every test run without Box, without a drive, and without credentials.

new.title: Run 01_box_inventory on Hanratty and post the numbers
new.body:
First real measurement of an actual accession. Folder `318353711369`, 485 files. Downloads nothing.

- [ ] Crawl completes
- [ ] **Numbers posted in this thread:** file count, total GB, duplicate %, zero-byte count, archive count, top 25 extensions
- [ ] Folder depth and size distribution recorded
- [ ] Outputs cleared before saving the notebook — it prints real filenames

### Read the results against two assumptions

- The design assumes **40–70% falls out at tier 0**. Expect much lower here. Most of that figure is OS and application files, and Box extracts contain none. **A low number is not evidence the assumption is wrong** — it is evidence we are measuring pre-filtered material.
- The gap analysis was built from a curated Box corpus. Any formats here that POC 2 never handled move those lanes up the priority order.

Notebook: [https://github.com/terbe2022/RIMS-Archival-Project-/blob/main/notebooks/01_box_inventory.ipynb](https://github.com/terbe2022/RIMS-Archival-Project-/blob/main/notebooks/01_box_inventory.ipynb)

new.title: Run inventory across all six accessions and compare
new.body:
Hanratty (485), Election_2016 (75), VCResearch (23), MichaelHart (8), DonCrummey (8), FemTech (0).

Six people's material. How much they **vary** is the design input — folder-context weighting only works if structure carries meaning consistently across accessions.

- [ ] All six crawled into per-source manifests
- [ ] Variation compared: folder depth, files per folder, extension spread
- [ ] `FemTech` (zero files) handled without error — empty folders are common on real drives
- [ ] Cross-accession duplicates surfaced via the shared content index

Watch for the same committee report appearing on four people's drives. That is genuinely useful to an archivist and completely invisible if accessions are processed in isolation.

new.title: Implement Stage 01 against the schema
new.body:
Walk, hash, identify — writing through `src/schema/manifest.py`, not ad hoc.

- [ ] `enforce()` used on every write; nothing bypasses the schema
- [ ] SHA-256 computed locally; Box SHA-1 retained in `content_sha1`
- [ ] Siegfried joined for `s01_puid`, `s01_format_name`, `s01_id_confidence`
- [ ] `s01_ext_mismatch` populated — this directly measures how wrong POC 2's extension routing was
- [ ] `path_flags` and `date_flags` populated
- [ ] 10,000 files in under a minute
- [ ] `validate.report()` passes

new.title: Write notebooks 02–04: triage filters, smart peek, scoring
new.body:
Logic goes in `src/`; notebooks import and explain it.

- [ ] `02_triage_free_filters` — duplicates, zero-byte, structural junk; reports the reduction %
- [ ] `03_smart_text_peek` — structured sampling compared against flat first-2KB on the same files
- [ ] `04_embeddings_and_scoring` — embed, score, folder-context weighting

Writes the `s02_*` columns. Keep `s02_file_score` and `s02_folder_score` separate — "included because its folder is 70% significant" is an auditable reason; a single blended number is not.

Depends on the manifest schema.

new.title: Write notebooks 05–06: model comparisons on T4
new.body:
Same samples, same prompts, three models each. This is what Colab's GPU is for.

- [ ] Three text models, same 20 documents
- [ ] Three vision models, same 20 images
- [ ] Ollama running as a background server in Colab
- [ ] Results posted to the corresponding model-comparison issues

Carry forward from POC 3: keep description and classification as **separate steps**. LLaVA described racialised content correctly while returning `offensive: false` — the description was right and the judgment was wrong. That split is why the semantic method worked.

new.title: Verify archive expansion against real archives
new.body:
The expander passes synthetic tests — nested zips, path traversal, password protection, compression-ratio bombs, corrupt files. It has never seen a real archive from an accession.

- [ ] Fetch a sample including archives
- [ ] Child rows carry correct `virtual_path`, `parent_uid`, `archive_depth`
- [ ] `validate.py` confirms parent references resolve
- [ ] Add py7zr / rarfile if `.7z` or `.rar` appear in the inventory
- [ ] `All Scanned Images.zip` (3.8 GB) as the large-archive case

new.title: Add Open in Colab badges and a notebooks README
new.body:
- [ ] Badge at the top of every notebook
- [ ] `notebooks/README.md` listing the series, what each does, what it depends on
- [ ] Repo README layout block updated with `notebooks/`, `src/`, `tests/`

Small, but it is the difference between Joanne being able to look at the work and not.

new.title: Confirm accession numbering with Joanne
new.body:
The Box folders are named `2620267_FemTech`, `2620191_MichaelHart`, `1513059_DonCrummey`, `2415001_VCResearch`. Those prefixes look like Archives accession numbers already in use.

The schema uses them as `source_id`, and **`file_uid` is derived from it**. So this is not cosmetic — getting it wrong means a full re-crawl of everything processed to that point.

- [ ] Confirm they are accession numbers
- [ ] Confirm the format and who assigns them
- [ ] Confirm what to use when an accession has no number yet

Reference: W1 schema, section 1.4

new.title: Decide where the PII mapping store lives
new.body:
POC 1 wrote the placeholder-to-real-value dictionary into a column beside the masked text. Convenient — and it defeats the entire point of masking.

Schema v1 keeps only `s04_pii_map_ref` in the manifest, pointing at a separate store.

- [ ] Where does that store live?
- [ ] Who can read it?
- [ ] Encryption at rest required?
- [ ] Retention — does the mapping outlive the processing run?

Blocks Stage 04.

new.title: How do accessions physically arrive
new.body:
Everything built so far assumes Box is the source. The six Box folders are **extracts copied from drives, not the drives** — so this probably is not how real accessions actually come in.

- [ ] What physically shows up when an accession arrives?
- [ ] Where is the media stored?
- [ ] Who is able to connect one to a machine?
- [ ] How many are queued, and in what condition is the media?
- [ ] Does anything warrant forensic imaging rather than a file copy?

If drives get mounted rather than uploaded, the source layer needs a filesystem path, and "download only what survives triage" no longer applies — a mounted drive is already local.

comments.2:
Partly unblocked. Box API access substitutes for physical drive access through the triage stages — `box_inventory.py` builds the manifest from Box metadata alone (name, size, sha1, path, timestamps), so inventory, deduplication and structural filtering all run before anything is downloaded. Colab verified working end to end.

**Still open, and the reason this stays blocked:** the six Box folders are extracts *copied from* drives, not the drives themselves. No OS or application files, folder structure possibly flattened, original filesystem metadata gone, and someone already made selection decisions we cannot see. So they cannot validate the tier-0 reduction rate or the format-mix assumptions.

See the W3 addendum. Split out as a separate issue: how accessions physically arrive.
